questions.question_text: An organization is developing a generative AI model to improve customer service. They need to ensure the model adheres to responsible AI practices, including bias and fairness considerations. Which TWO of the following actions should they take? (Select TWO)
options: A. Deploy the model without any regulatory or ethical considerations to focus on performance.
B. Establish an AI center of excellence and A model governance committee to ensure ethical guidance and compliance.
C. Use AWS S3 for storing the raw data used in training the model without any data curation or diversity checks.
D. Implement bertscore as a metric to evaluate the quality of generated text output.
E. Conduct regular audits and monitoring of the AI system for ensuring fairness and preventing bias.
questions.explanation:
A. INCORRECT - Deploying the model without regulatory or ethical considerations is not a responsible approach and can lead to legal risks, biased outputs, and loss of customer trust.

B. CORRECT - Establishing an AI center of excellence (AI CoE) and a model governance committee ensures that ethical guidelines and compliance are maintained throughout the development process.

C. INCORRECT - Using AWS S3 for storing raw data without curation or diversity checks can lead to biased datasets, which can result in unfair outcomes from the generative AI model.

D. INCORRECT - While BERTScore is a useful metric for evaluating text quality, it does not address bias and fairness considerations that are critical for responsible AI practices.

E. CORRECT - Regular audits and monitoring of the AI system help ensure fairness and prevent bias by continuously assessing the performance and impact of the model.

questions.question_text: An e-commerce company wants to implement a recommendation system that predicts which products customers are likely to purchase based on their browsing history. The system should be scalable, cost-effective, and capable of handling large volumes of data without manual intervention. Which AWS service combination would best meet these requirements?
options: A. Amazon SageMaker for model training and hosting, Amazon Kinesis for real-time data streaming
B. Amazon Redshift for data warehousing, AWS Lambda for batch processing
C. Amazon EC2 instances for model training and hosting, Amazon S3 for storage
D. Amazon Aurora for database management, Amazon API Gateway for API deployment
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is A: Amazon SageMaker for model training and hosting, Amazon Kinesis for real-time data streaming. Amazon SageMaker provides a managed service that enables developers to build, train, and deploy machine learning models at scale with minimal infrastructure setup and management. It supports both batch and real-time inferencing, which aligns well with the company's needs. Additionally, it integrates seamlessly with other AWS services such as Kinesis for handling large volumes of streaming data in near real-time, ensuring scalability and cost-effectiveness without manual intervention.

Option B (Amazon Redshift for data warehousing, AWS Lambda for batch processing) is not suitable because Amazon Redshift is designed for data warehousing and analytics rather than machine learning model training. AWS Lambda can be used for batch processing but lacks the comprehensive machine learning capabilities of SageMaker.

Option C (Amazon EC2 instances for model training and hosting, Amazon S3 for storage) requires manual management of EC2 instances, which increases operational costs and complexity compared to SageMaker's managed service. While it does provide a way to store data in Amazon S3, the overall solution is less cost-effective and scalable.

Option D (Amazon Aurora for database management, Amazon API Gateway for API deployment) focuses on database management and API deployment but does not address the core requirements of building and deploying machine learning models.

questions.question_text: Select the best answer. Your company is planning to use a generative AI model to improve customer support by generating personalized responses based on user queries. You need to ensure the model can handle high traffic during peak hours and provide accurate responses in real-time while keeping costs under control.
options: A. Deploy the AI model using Amazon SageMaker with an Auto Scaling group for handling variable traffic and use AWS Lambda for real-time processing.
B. Use Amazon EC2 instances to host the AI model, maintaining a fixed number of instances during peak hours.
C. Implement the AI model on-premises with local servers to ensure low latency and high performance.
D. Deploy the AI model using Amazon S3 for storage and AWS Lambda for processing queries.
questions.explanation: Option A is the best choice as it leverages Auto Scaling within Amazon SageMaker, which dynamically adjusts the number of instances based on traffic demands, ensuring cost efficiency. Additionally, AWS Lambda can handle real-time requests efficiently without requiring a fixed infrastructure setup. Option B involves static EC2 instances, which may lead to underutilization during off-peak times and overprovisioning during peak hours, increasing costs. On-premises deployment (Option C) is not scalable or cost-effective for this use case due to the need for additional hardware and maintenance. Option D uses S3 for storage but lacks a real-time processing solution, making it unsuitable for generating responses in real-time.
